cases.customer_question: Does an existing Class 1 RF qualification report remain valid when RF PHY testing must be repeated for other PHY modes?
question_variants: Can existing RF reports still be reused?
Is RF retesting required after RF PHY failure?
Do all RF tests need to be rerun after PHY issues?
Can prior Class 1 RF evidence remain valid?
Is only RF PHY retest necessary?
cases.actual_issue: Clarifying whether previously passed RF qualification evidence can still be reused after discovering RF PHY output power issues during additional PHY mode testing.
cases.plain_english_explanation: Bluetooth qualification separates some RF and RF PHY test evidence categories. Even if one PHY mode or configuration fails, some previously completed RF evidence may still remain valid if the original requirements were satisfied. This can reduce retesting scope.
cases.consultant_answer: The consultant explained that RF PHY retesting was mandatory because the DUT had effectively operated at Class 2 output levels during testing. However, the consultant also stated that the existing RF test report for the Class 1 RF requirements remained valid and did not require re-execution. Only the RF PHY qualification evidence needed correction and retesting.
cases.decision_logic: Bluetooth qualification may permit reuse of previously valid RF test evidence if the applicable RF requirements were already satisfied, even when RF PHY qualification evidence must be corrected separately.
cases.final_recommendation: Determine whether the issue affects RF PHY evidence only or also invalidates existing RF reports before scheduling full retesting. Reuse previously valid RF evidence whenever qualification rules permit.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: Assuming all RF evidence must be repeated can create unnecessary test cost and schedule delays. Conversely, incorrectly reusing invalid RF evidence may lead to rejected submissions.
